tags.name: Valdovų rūmai
tags.name:en: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania

voyage.name: Gediminas Castle
voyage.content: This is the Upper Castle of a complex of three built from the 13th century, much bashed about, and abandoned from the 16th. (The Lower Castle became the site of the Arsenal, Palace and Cathedral, and the "Crooked Castle" was destroyed in 1394.) You can ascend the cobbled lane and enter the courtyard free for views of the city, and the Three Crosses on the hill east. The ducal palace east side of the courtyard is just

voyage.name: Old Arsenal
voyage.content: This arsenal in the Lower Castle was built in the 15th century and stored heavy artillery. It's now part of the National Museum, displaying the country's pre-history and early history until the arrival of Christianity in the 11th century.

voyage.name: Museum of Applied Arts & Design
voyage.content: This arsenal in the Lower Castle was built in the 15th century and stored heavy artillery. It's now part of the National Museum, displaying the country's pre-history and early history until the arrival of Christianity in the 11th century.

voyage.name: New Arsenal
voyage.content: The New Arsenal was established in the 18th century and mostly served as a barracks. It's now part of the National Museum displaying Lithuania's history and cultural heritage. As of October 2025, it is closed for major restructuring work.

voyage.name: Vilnius Cathedral
voyage.alt: Basilica of St Stanislaus and St Ladislaus of Vilnius
voyage.content: The first cathedral was built here in 1251, reverting to pagan worship in 1263. Fire destroyed a second in 1419, a third in 1530 and a fourth in 1610. Many parts of the fifth survive, notably the baroque chapel of St Casimir, but much was lost when the south tower collapsed in 1769 — did those pagans have a friend on high? What you see now is mostly the neo-classical structure completed in 1801. The crypt has a displ

voyage.name: Palace of the Grand Dukes of Lithuania
voyage.content: This is a modern replica: the original was built in the 15th century, ruined in the 17th and demolished in 1801. A merchant's house was then built, which became part of the Arsenal. In the 1990s after independence the palace was rebuilt to the original plan, somehow without deciding what it would be used for, and to outcry as it blocked the vista from Cathedral Square. It's become part of the National Museum, with di

voyage.name: Presidential Palace
voyage.content: An 18th-century palace which is the seat of the President of Lithuania. Guided tours are available at weekends, and the palace is also open to the public on Open House days.

voyage.name: Toy Museum
voyage.content: Interactive museum of toys down the ages, child-friendly of course.

voyage.name: Vilnius University
voyage.content: Vilnius University now has faculties across the city and beyond, but this is the baroque core of it, with the library, courtyards, observatory and Church of St Johns (plural: Šv Jono, the Baptist and the Evangelist). You can see the church, four courtyards and Franciszek Smuglewicz Hall free, and guided tours are available for groups of four or more by prior booking. The Adam Mickiewicz Museum displays the university

voyage.name: House of the Signatories
voyage.content: Neo-renaissance mansion where Lithuania's Act of Independence was signed on 16 February 1918. It's now a branch of the National Museum depicting the story of Lithuania as a separate nation, in which independent spirit it makes few concessions to non-speakers of the language.

voyage.name: Church Heritage Museum
voyage.content: Displays religious art.

voyage.name: National Museum of Art
voyage.content: Huge display of art from the 14th to 20th century.

voyage.name: Museums Centre for Information, Digitisation and LIMIS
voyage.content: About the digitisation and online curating of museum collections. So if you want to grasp the "principles of the use of ontologies" you've come to the right place, but if you seek physical exhibits you've not been listening.

voyage.name: Culinary Museum
voyage.content: This is about tableware rather than cuisine.

voyage.name: St Nicholas Church
voyage.alt: Šv. Nikolajaus Stebukladario palaikų Pernešimo cerkvė
voyage.content: A Russian Orthodox church. Not to be confused with the RC St Nicholas on Šv Mikalojaus.

voyage.name: Kazys Varnelis House-Museum
voyage.content: Varnelis (1917-2020) was an abstract artist who mostly lived in the USA, returning to Vilnius in 1998. His house is now part of National Museum, displaying his studio and works.

voyage.name: Town Hall
voyage.content: The present town hall is neoclassical, built 1799. It's used for civic events, and the simplest way to see inside is to attend a concert or similar, which may be free. The square is a venue for fairs, concerts, demos and so on.

voyage.name: Contemporary Art Centre
voyage.content: This has a permanent display of Fluxus artwork plus other rotating exhibitions.

voyage.name: Vilnius Museum
voyage.content: Small independent museum of city history.

voyage.name: Museum of Illusions
voyage.content: Ames Room, Pepper's Ghost, holograms, all the staples are here. Children will love it.

voyage.name: Church of St Casimir
voyage.content: Baroque RC church completed in 1618. It's been held by various faiths (including a spell as Museum of Atheism) but was re-consecrated in 1991. It often hosts organ recitals.

voyage.name: Bastion of Vilnius Defensive Wall
voyage.content: The city walls were built 1503-22 with nine gates (of which only Gate of Dawn survives) and this artillery position. It's now a museum of the city's military history.

voyage.name: Orthodox Church of the Holy Spirit
voyage.content: Re-built in 1753 in Baroque / Rococo. It's affiliated to the Monastery of the Holy Spirit and the Convent of Saint Mary Magdalen, with services in Russian.

voyage.name: St Nicholas Church
voyage.content: The Roman Catholic St Nick's, brick gothic, and the oldest church in Vilnius being documented in 1387.

voyage.name: Holy Trinity Church
voyage.content: Part of a Ukrainian Greek Catholic monastery, and mostly built in the early 17th century.

voyage.name: Church of St Theresa
voyage.content: Just north of the Gate of Dawn (indeed serving as the entrance to get up to the gate's Virgin Mary icon) is a Roman Catholic church popular with worshippers also outside mass, completed in 1650.

voyage.name: Gate of Dawn
voyage.content: The last survivor of the walled city's nine gates, various called Medininkai Gate as the street led south to that village, Sharp Gate, and now Gate of Dawn. It's straddled by a chapel with a large icon of the Virgin Mary, painted in the 1620s, which has become a pilgrimage destination. Mass is held daily in Lithuanian and Polish. Enter the chapel via the Church of St Theresa, just follow the head-scarves. When the ch

voyage.name: St Anne's Church
voyage.content: Small flamboyant church in Gothic style, built by 1500 and little altered since. There is a legend that when Napoleon's campaigns brought him to Vilnius, he declared that he'd like to lift the church on his palm and carry it back to Paris. (Obviously untrue, since given the horrors of his retreat, he'd have been forced to eat it before he reached Warsaw.) St Anne's is not within Užupis but backs onto the river bounda

voyage.name: Church of St Francis and St Bernard
voyage.content: Also known as the Bernadine Church, it is next to St Anne's on the riverbank. It's a sturdy Gothic building from the 16th century, incorporated into the city walls, with loopholes toshoot at the Cossacks.

voyage.name: Cathedral of the Theotokos
voyage.alt: Dievo Motinos Ėmimo į Dangų katedra
voyage.content: Like St Anne's, this stands by an entrance bridge to Užupis. It was first built in the 1340s by Grand Duke Algirdas before the country became Christian. It's been destroyed, rebuilt and changed use several times - in the 1820s it was the university anatomy department. The present building is from the 1860s in sort-of neoclassical meets the Byzantine style of Georgia. It's Eastern Orthodox (which calls the Virgin Mary

voyage.name: Angel of Uzupis
voyage.content: In the main square is a statue unveiled on 1 April 2002 of Gabriel blowing a trumpet. He's probably blowing a raspberry.

voyage.name: Tartle
voyage.content: Gallery of modern art, visit only by pre-booked guided tour.

voyage.name: Bernadine Cemetery
voyage.content: Established in 1810 by the Bernardine monks of the Church of St Francis in Užupis. It became the main city cemetery, with some 14,000 burial plots, but fell into disrepair from 1945. It was restored from 2010.

voyage.name: Three Crosses Hill
voyage.content: A monument to seven Franciscan friars supposedly beheaded here by pagans, while seven more were crucified then thrown in the river. The story is nonsense, but Lithuania was the last European country to convert to Christianity, and there was indeed conflict. King Mindaugas was baptised in 1250 but the country as a whole didn't convert until 1485 when the Duchy united with Poland. Wooden crosses have been erected on th

voyage.name: Old Jewish Cemetery
voyage.content: In use from 1828 to the 1940s - though it was called "New Cemetery" as the first (north of River Neris) was established in the 15th century. The Soviets made sure to destroy both plus the synagogue, so what remains here is a memorial made of old tombstones. A new-new cemetery is now in the northwest district of Šeškinė.

voyage.name: Church of Saints Peter and Paul
voyage.content: The first church from around 1500 was wooden and burned down, and its successor was wrecked in the 1650s in the war with Russia. The present building was commissioned by Michał Kazimierz Pac (1624-82), begun in 1668 but only completed in 1704 after his death. The exterior is fairly plain, but inside is baroque run riot.

voyage.name: Saulės Cemetery
voyage.content: The 19th century graveyard 500 m east of St Peter & St Paul, tightly packed with the funerary art of the city's notables. It's atmospheric going on unkempt, and the two chapels are in a poor state. Its name means "sunny" but it was only called this from 1945, from the adjacent Saulės gatve.

voyage.name: Pushkin Museum
voyage.content: Alexander Pushkin (1799-1837) was often in exile around the edges of Russia: not here, but his son lived in this mansion. His works were translated into Lithuanian and much of the museum is about that literary task, but it has period decor.

voyage.name: Markučiai Park
voyage.content: This green area stretches east of the Pushkin Museum, linking with others such as Pavilnys Regional Park to form a greenbelt between the city and its industrial and commuter suburbs. The parks have bosky walks and are dotted with ancient burial tumuli.

voyage.name: Railway Museum
voyage.content: Presents the history of railways in Lithuania from Prussian times until today. Railway equipment small enough to fit into a room, tickets, staff uniforms and the like are on display in addition to scale models, pictures and videos. Child-friendly.

voyage.name: Franciscan Monastery
voyage.content: Founded in 1334 and it's their monks who are commemorated by the Three Crosses. It's in shabby condition, but you can access the church daily 07:00-22:30.

voyage.name: Church of Vytautas the Great
voyage.content: It's Roman Catholic, redbrick Gothic, dating to 1400 but 19th century in its present form. Also known as the Church of the Assumption.

voyage.name: Vilna Gaon Jewish State Museum
voyage.content: Early modern Lithuania (like Poland, "White Russia" and Ukraine) had a large Jewish population, as Russia's Jews were encouraged (often violently) to live in the western "Pale of Settlement". Best known is the rabbinical scholar Elijah ben Solomon Zalman (1720-97), the "Vilna Gaon". The museum describes that community, its tribulations and eventual obliteration.

voyage.name: MO Museum
voyage.content: Museum with modern contemporary art and changing exhibitions.

voyage.name: Frank Zappa bust
voyage.content: Frank Zappa (1940-1993) is commemorated by a bust on Kalinausko gatve. He was never here, but local fans erected it in 1995, donating a replica to Baltimore, Maryland, his childhood home.

voyage.name: Church of St Constantine and St Michael
voyage.content: This orthodox church was built in 1913 to mark the 300th anniversary of the Romanov dynasty, much good it did them. It's a dinky onion-domed building.

voyage.name: Lithuanian Theatre, Music and Cinema Museum
voyage.content: Has little for non-speakers of Lithuanian, though some exhibits transcend language.

voyage.name: Money Museum
voyage.content: History of money, and collection of coins and bills from around the world.

voyage.name: Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights
voyage.content: This is in the former KGB headquarters, where over 1000 were put to death. In spite of the plurals, it is specifically the Lithuanian experience under Soviet rule that is described; the experience under Nazism would reveal a very dark corner of national history. And until 2018, it was called the Museum of Genocide Victims, yet almost entirely omitted the genocide against what had been a large Jewish population. Just

voyage.name: Church of St Philip and St Jacob
voyage.alt: Šv Apaštalų Pilypo ir Jokūbo bažnyčia
voyage.content: Red and white Baroque church of the Dominican order, completed in 1722. It houses a large icon of the Virgin Mary "Hodegetria" - in iconography this means "shows the way" as she points to the infant as the salvation of mankind.

voyage.name: Seimas Palace
voyage.content: This complex houses the Lithuanian parliament. The first building, completed in 1980, was the seat of the Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic, and looks it. In 2007 the new Parliament Hall (or Building 2) was opened. Building 3 was added to house committees and technical services. Exhibitions in Building 2 are open to the public daily 08:00-17:00, and those in Building 1 on Fridays 11:00-15:00. You can also book a g

voyage.name: Vingis Park
voyage.content: Bounds city centre to the west, large and wooded so you could easily lose a small child. It's in a loop of River Neris ("vingis" means bend or curve) and together with other parks north and woodland downriver creates a greenbelt on this side. Enter from the east along Čiurlionio gatve, which spans the busy ring-road: there's a multinational military cemetery by the entrance. The palace has long been demolished - in 1

voyage.name: Church of St Catherine
voyage.content: Built in the 18th century in Baroque style and dedicated to Saint Catherine of Alexandria, as part of a Benedictine Nunnery. The church is known for its elegant façade, intricate stucco decorations, but many of its artworks were either lost in WW2 or moved to the Lithuanian National Museum of Art.

voyage.name: Vilnius TV tower
voyage.content: The 326.5 m high telecommunications tower was completed in 1980 and is visible from far and wide. You can ride the lift to the restaurant and observation deck. In 2022 / 23 construction work is under way but the place remains open.

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of the Sign
voyage.content: Built in Neo-Byzantine style in 1903, this is the Eastern Orthodox church you see when looking west along Gedimino prospekt. It was financed by fundraising around the Russian Empire.

voyage.name: New City Centre
voyage.content: The modern business district, in Šnipiškės north of the river. Its 21st century glass and steel skyscrapers are visible from afar, including the 148 m Europa Tower.

voyage.name: Energy and Technology Museum
voyage.content: This was the city's first power plant, opened in 1903. It exhibits electricity generation, industrial technologies, child-friendly interactions and transformation, the Tesla-inspired wizardry that enables long-distance transmission of electricity. They also have an Escape Room, €50 for 2-4 players.

voyage.name: Suderve Cemetery
voyage.content: Most of it is Roman Catholic burials but the north end is Jewish, with re-interments from other destroyed cemeteries. These include the scholar Vilna Gaon.

voyage.name: Rasos Cemetery
voyage.content: The main resting place of 20th century notables. It holds the heart of Józef Piłsudski (1867–1935), founder of independent Poland, with the rest of him in Wawel in Kraków.

voyage.name: Museum of the Centre of Europe
voyage.content: Open-air sculpture park. It's within Europas Park, the rest of which is free and open to dusk.

voyage.name: Lithuanian Opera and Ballet Theatre
voyage.content: Grand ornate opera house with three or four weekly performances.

voyage.name: Oskaras Koršunovas Theatre (OKT)
voyage.content: Avant garde theatre southwest edge of Old Town,.

voyage.name: Old Theatre of Vilnius
voyage.content: Creaky but atmospheric old theatre with performances mostly in Russian.

voyage.name: Lindyhop Klubas
voyage.content: Lindy Hop is a US swing / jazz dance style that evolved from the 1930s and is now enjoying a revival, with clubs and lessons, retro gear optional.

voyage.name: Halės turgus
voyage.content: The main market hall of Vilnius, built in 1906 and looking like a railway terminus. Inside, its east side has food stalls and a couple of eateries. Adjacent is the modern wing for clothing and household wares.

voyage.name: Akropolis
voyage.content: Large mall with multiplex cinema and ice rink.

voyage.name: Centro pasažas
voyage.content: Small mall west edge of Old Town.

voyage.name: Europa
voyage.content: Opened in 2004, when Lithuania joined EU.

voyage.name: GO9
voyage.content: Central mall with a large branch of H&M.

voyage.name: Helios City
voyage.content: With a branch of Iki.

voyage.name: Ozas
voyage.content: One of the biggest shopping malls in Vilnius, many stores and services plus Multikino cinema.

voyage.name: Panorama
voyage.content: Multi-level centre west of business district.

voyage.name: Outlet Park
voyage.content: Shopping mall for discount stores.

voyage.name: CUP
voyage.content: Trading since 1974.

voyage.name: Vegafè
voyage.content: Vegan cafe.

voyage.name: Pilies kepyklėlė
voyage.content: Café-bakery in the university building near Saints John.

voyage.name: Kamikadzė Japonų virtuvė
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant with the usual offerings.

voyage.name: Plus Plus Plus Gastrobaras
voyage.content: This is the most central of a fast-food chain.

voyage.name: Dėvėti
voyage.content: Calls itself a gastropub, more like a bar with pizza and pita bread sandwiches.

voyage.name: RadhaRane
voyage.content: Vegetarian Indian restaurant with a good menu choice.

voyage.name: Wok to Walk
voyage.content: This is the main outlet of an Asian cuisine franchise.

voyage.name: Fėjų kepyklėlė
voyage.content: Bakery-cafe with pastries, snacks, pizza and ice cream. It's infested with Lithuanian fairies, which you'll either adore or upchuck over.

voyage.name: Buga Sotu
voyage.content: Trad food: chicken, dumplings, kibinai, pizzas and carp. Live music on Friday and sometimes on Saturday. You'd most likely eat here if you visited the TV Tower and baulked at their restaurant prices.

voyage.name: Amatininkų užeiga
voyage.content: Lithuanian and international food.

voyage.name: Cozy
voyage.content: Well-named place, with laid-back restaurant upstairs, DJ-bar downstairs, serves hearty modern food with a few vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Mint Vinetu
voyage.content: Independent bookstore and coffee shop.

voyage.name: Fortas
voyage.content: This is the original of what has become a chain. They do pub-style food with theme days on different nations' cuisines. Other outlets are at Vilniaus 18 in Old Town and Konstitucijos pr 7A north of the river.

voyage.name: Mano Guru
voyage.content: Mostly vegetarian food, and no alcohol. All the staff are former drug misusers.

voyage.name: Vapiano
voyage.content: Italian style, fast casual restaurant (part of the German global chain). Tasty salads, à la carte pastas and pizzas are made in front of the guest.

voyage.name: Medininkai
voyage.content: Lithuanian food near Gate of Dawn, it got good reviews to 2022 but now feels tourist-trappy.

voyage.name: Sakwa
voyage.content: Café in a two-storey building, retro-styled like a suburban house. Lithuanian, Polish and European cuisine.

voyage.name: Fabai
voyage.content: Vilnius doesn't have much by way of Caucasus cuisine, so it may be worth the trip out to this bar grill - and you'll have to queue at peak times. It's styled like a country tavern, with grillroom, ballroom, bar, and two billiard halls.

voyage.name: Belmontas Cafe
voyage.content: Folk-themed outdoor restaurant by a 19th century mill and waterfall.

voyage.name: Balzac
voyage.content: Traditional French cuisine, well prepared, great atmosphere.

voyage.name: Bistro 18
voyage.content: Small restaurant and wine bar with good selection of European cuisine.

voyage.name: Čagino
voyage.content: Named for the architect Nikolai Chagin (1823-1909) who designed several churches in Vilnius and led a revival of the Byzantine style. It's Russian food and their occasional gimmick is dinner in the dark, check ahead for these dates.

voyage.name: Da Antonio
voyage.content: Excellent upscale Italian food.

voyage.name: La Provence
voyage.content: Grand French dining in a classic interior.

voyage.name: Lokys
voyage.content: Specializes in Lithuanian traditional cuisine and game.

voyage.name: Markus ir Ko
voyage.content: Steakhouse with music.

voyage.name: Vanille Lounge
voyage.content: Upmarket seasonal European fare.

voyage.name: Kiras
voyage.content: Café in 1970s style, with happy memories of Soviet days: "chaika" a tea-house is a pun on "cheka" the secret police. They have another café at Pylimo 21b.

voyage.name: Alaus Namai
voyage.content: Big saloon offering beer from less-known Lithuanian brands.

voyage.name: Artistai
voyage.content: The large courtyard is a great place to relax and watch the sunset. Friendly service, live music.

voyage.name: Šnekutis
voyage.content: Long-table like a beer hall, with trad beer and food.

voyage.name: BIX
voyage.content: Bar founded by BIX rock band. Live rock / metal bands on Friday nights, karaoke on Thursdays, and rock music any time on the dance floor. Surprisingly good food.

voyage.name: Soho Club
voyage.content: LGBT club, gets very crowded.

voyage.name: Filaretai Hostel
voyage.content: Chilled out place in "Republic of Užupis". Self-service kitchen, washing machine, WiFi sitting-room with free computers and TV.

voyage.name: Jimmy Jumps House
voyage.content: Friendly, well-run hostel with 4, 6 and 8-bedded dorms, as well as "twin rooms" with single bunk beds for two people.

voyage.name: Pogo Hostel
voyage.content: Good value hostel in a great location, helpful staff. Four dorms of 6 beds and two private rooms.

voyage.name: City Hotel Algirdas
voyage.content: Simple Scandinavian style hotel in the centre.

voyage.name: Domus Maria
voyage.content: Secluded 48-room hotel within a former Carmelite convent, you sleep in the nuns' cells.

voyage.name: Ibis Vilnius Centre
voyage.content: Standard boxy Ibis 500 m north of Cathedral Square, clean and good value.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn
voyage.content: Clean modern chain hotel in Business District.

voyage.name: Congress
voyage.content: Older hotel by riverside, friendly and comfy, some street noise.

voyage.name: Courtyard by Marriott
voyage.content: Reliable mid-price chain hotel. 12-room hotel.

voyage.name: Vilnius City Hotel
voyage.content: Simple 26-room hotel with free parking, some fittings in need of repair.

voyage.name: Ratonda Centrum Hotels
voyage.content: 43-room hotel with sauna, fitness centre and meeting rooms, close to parliament.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn
voyage.content: Modern glassy place, clean and comfy.

voyage.name: Best Western
voyage.content: Great value mid-price hotel near Parliament.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Kempinski
voyage.content: Now you've arrived. Stylish, mostly modern interior with 96 rooms, spa, restaurant and conference facilities.

voyage.name: Mabre Residence Hotel
voyage.content: This 40-room hotel is in a neoclassical Orthodox Monastery, dating back 500 years but rebuilt in 1995. High walls give it an exclusive feel. Sauna, fitness center, and pool. Some guests found rooms poky and mediocre quality.

voyage.name: Novotel Vilnius Centre
voyage.content: Modern 159-room hotel, clean and spacious, close to Opera House and Cathedral square.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Royal Astorija Hotel
voyage.content: Splendid place in the heart of old town, US President George W Bush and Britain's Prince Charles (now king) have enjoyed the great service offered here.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel Lietuva
voyage.content: High-rise by the river with 291 rooms and conference facilities, great reviews. The even-numbered rooms have views over old town, also from the top-floor Skybar.

voyage.name: Narutis Hotel
voyage.content: Stylish upmarket place by the university. The restaurant gets good reviews.

voyage.name: Imperial Hotel
voyage.content: This has left the Ramada chain and gone upmarket. Good scores for comfort and dining.

voyage.name: Stikliai Hotel
voyage.content: "Stikliai" means glasses and it's in an old glassworks, charmingly converted, and now part of Relais & Chateaux group.

voyage.name: Neringa Hotel
voyage.content: Slick 60-room hotel with sauna, fitness centre, wi-fi, pool, bar. Some street noise.

voyage.name: Shakespeare Hotel
voyage.content: Charming 31-room English country-style hotel. Rooms are named after famous writers - he's called Šekspyras in Lithuanian.

voyage.name: Park Inn by Radisson Vilnius Airport Hotel
voyage.content: Modern place with 120 rooms, Italian restaurant and fitness centre. It's just ten minutes walk to the airport terminal.
